info.title: FlashData Customer API
info.description: Google search, YouTube data and media downloads, with endpoints for jobs, accounts, API keys and billing. See /docs for request examples and setup guides.

get.summary: Verify current API key ownership and recurring readiness
get.description: Free header-only API-key read. Returns public account/key IDs and authoritative ownership. No request body. Does not alter the existing /api-access metadata response. Shares the 120/minute account-read limit. Fail closed on unavailability; do not infer ownership from key prefix, plan, or local state. No query parameters are accepted. Responses are no-store.

200.description: Verify current API key ownership and recurring readiness

post.summary: Create an opaque Web session
post.description:
Sets the Secure, HttpOnly `__Host-fd_session` cookie. Pending accounts
receive a restricted email_verification Session for the verification dashboard.
Eligible verified accounts receive their one-time Trial Credits on login if not already granted.
An active account
receives a full Session unless its migrated identity still requires a
current legal acceptance, in which case it receives a restricted
legal_acceptance Session. An account with a scheduled deletion request
receives a restricted deletion_recovery Session. Accounts whose deletion
is processing/failed/completed, and suspended accounts, receive 403.

post.summary: Revoke the current session

get.summary: Read the current account and user
Get the CSRF token bound to the current session

post.summary: Request or resend an email verification message
post.description: For every syntactically valid email, returns the same response regardless of whether the account is missing, pending, active, suspended, or deleted. Eligible pending accounts receive a rotated one-time link after the resend cooldown.

post.summary: Verify an email and activate the account
post.description: Atomically consumes the one-time token and activates the Account and User. Existing account and trial-credit rules apply. Without a signup Session the user logs in explicitly. An allowed-origin request carrying the matching signup Session and its X-CSRF-Token may receive a rotated Session cookie for the same verified account; a verification token alone never signs in a user.

post.summary: Continue the original signup session after email verification
post.description: Requires an allowed Origin and the CSRF token bound to a live password-authenticated email-verification Session. Returns pending until that Session's own account is verified, including verification in another browser. Atomically revokes the signup Session and issues a fresh full or legal-acceptance Session. Does not accept an account ID, email, password or verification token, bypass legal acceptance, or grant credits.

202.description: Email verification is pending; no new Session

post.summary: Request a password reset email
post.description: Always returns the same 202 response for a syntactically valid email regardless of account existence or lifecycle state. Only eligible active or locked identities receive mail.

post.summary: Set a new password and revoke existing sessions
post.description: Atomically consumes the password-reset token, stores a new Argon2id credential, revokes every existing Session, and invalidates other password-reset tokens. It does not log the user in or create a Session.

get.summary: List active sessions for the current user

delete.summary: Revoke all sessions except the current one

204.description: Session revoked. If it was the current Session, the cookie is cleared.

post.summary: Verify the current password for a sensitive operation
post.description: Records a short-lived recent-auth proof on the current server-side session.

patch.summary: Change the password and rotate the current session

204.description: Password changed; current session rotated and other sessions revoked when requested

get.summary: Read account settings

delete.summary: Schedule account deletion and revoke all existing sessions and API Keys
delete.description: Administrator accounts must have their platform role revoked through the audited operator workflow before deletion can be scheduled. A unique active deletion request is the natural idempotency boundary. Concurrent authenticated schedules return the same request. After Session revocation, a lost response is recovered by logging into deletion_recovery mode and reading GET /account/deletion; revoked Sessions are never accepted for replay.

202.description: Deletion scheduled; active sessions and keys revoked

get.summary: Read the current account deletion request

delete.summary: Cancel a scheduled deletion during the grace period
delete.description: Uses a scheduled-to-cancelled compare-and-set. A processor race returns 409; after success the recovery Session is rotated and cannot replay the old transition.

204.description: Deletion cancelled, account reactivated, and recovery Session rotated according to the legal-acceptance gate

200.description: Legal acceptance recorded and Session rotated to full mode

post.summary: Create a replacement key and schedule old-key revocation
post.description: Creates a new key and keeps the old key active until revokeOldAt. By default, the overlap lasts 24 hours or until the old key expires, whichever is earlier. A custom revokeOldAt must be in the future, within seven days, and no later than the old key expiry.

revokeOldAt.description: Optional old-key revocation time; defaults to 24 hours and cannot exceed seven days or the old key expiry.

get.summary: Read the effective Stripe subscription

post.summary: Create a Stripe-hosted Checkout Session
post.description: Subscriptions and published credit packs use priceId. A custom top-up uses amountMinor instead (USD cents, $10 to $999,999.99); the server calculates credits at the fixed credit value and creates a private one-time Stripe price. Product, provider price, currency, success URL and cancel URL are never accepted from the browser. Credits are granted only after a verified paid event for the quoted amount.

amountMinor.description: Custom top-up amount in USD cents.

post.summary: Upgrade the current Stripe subscription to a higher published price
post.description: The server verifies that the FlashData price is active, available in the current livemode, USD-denominated, recurring, the same interval, and strictly more expensive than the current subscription price. Product, provider price, currency and proration options are never accepted from the browser. Local entitlement and credits change only after a verified provider event is projected.

post.summary: Create a Stripe Customer Portal Session
Schedule or undo cancellation of the current paid subscription
post.description: Setting cancelAtPeriodEnd to true schedules cancellation at the current billing period end; false keeps the subscription. Entitlements update after a verified Stripe subscription event. This endpoint never cancels immediately or issues a refund.

200.description: One-time payment history without provider secrets

get.summary: Read the calling API key's authorized sources and result origin
get.description:
Free, header-only X-API-Key authentication. Returns only granted public
source names and the configured signed-result storage origin (null if
unavailable). No account ID, key ID, secret or storage credentials are returned.
Local MCP revalidates this endpoint before every tool discovery and call,
including cached result reads. No query parameters or request body are accepted.
All /api-access routes share 120 requests per minute per client IP and return
Cache-Control private, no-store. Normal key last-used tracking still occurs.

200.description: Authorized public sources and result origin

429.description: Too many account reads; retry after the rate-limit window

get.summary: Read the live account balance using an API key
get.description: Read the current credit balance shared by all API keys in your account. Active reservations can reduce the available balance. This request costs no Credits and takes no query parameters or body. Responses are private and are not cached; account-read rate limits apply.

200.description: Signed balance and nonnegative available Credits

429.description: Too many account reads; retry after the rate-limit window

get.summary: Read actual account prices for sources authorized by the API key
get.description: Read your account rates for sources allowed by the API key. A null price means that source is unavailable. request_count counts queries, not returned items; download rates are per TB (10^12 bytes). Estimates do not reserve Credits or capacity. This request costs no Credits. Responses are private and are not cached; account-read rate limits apply.

parameters.name: source
parameters.description: A source granted to this key; omit to read all granted sources.

parameters.name: request_count
parameters.description: Decimal integer number of calls; does not estimate download size.

429.description: Too many account reads; retry after the rate-limit window

get.summary: Read account plan limits and current pending jobs using an API key
get.description: Read your concurrency, batch-size and pending-job limits, plus the current pending count. These values help plan requests but do not reserve capacity. This request costs no Credits and takes no query parameters or body. Responses are private and are not cached; account-read rate limits apply.

200.description: Plan ceilings and current pending count

429.description: Too many account reads; retry after the rate-limit window

get.summary: Read account usage for sources authorized by the API key
get.description:
Free read, authenticated only by X-API-Key. Includes all account keys but
only sources granted to the calling key. Does not return query text, keys,
payment details or other accounts. Defaults to seven days; maximum 31 days.
Dates must use UTC Z timestamps. From is inclusive and to exclusive;
both are rounded down to minutes. With from alone, to defaults to from + 7 days.
With neither, to is the start of the next minute. Aggregates are eventually
consistent; even updating=false does not guarantee all recent events are ingested.
Read limit: 60 requests per minute per client IP.

parameters.name: source
parameters.description: An exact catalog source granted to the calling key; omitted means all granted sources.

200.description: Scoped request counts and charged Credits, with freshness information

429.description: Too many usage reads; retry after the rate-limit window

query.description: Source request body. In batch mode, also accepts an object containing only queries, an array of 1 to 20 request bodies. Every entry must match the selected source and its input schema. Search and Suggestions require query; Channel requires handle; Metadata, Transcript, Captions, Trainability and Download require an 11-character video_id matching [A-Za-z0-9_-]. Download batch entries must supply params.storage for customer storage; console browser delivery is not supported in this envelope. Account batch and pending-job limits still apply.

get.summary: Download a completed async result
get.description: By default, authenticates access and redirects to a short-lived private R2 URL; clients receive the original JSON directly from R2. Accept: text/plain independently returns HTTP 200 with the original result fields as indented plain text. X-Respond-With: markdown selects Markdown content: application/json wraps it in content alongside the original metadata, replacing results; text/plain returns metadata followed by Markdown. Missing Accept or a global wildcard defaults to JSON. Formatting does not submit another query or charge query credits. Stored results expire 24 hours after completion. Errors remain structured JSON.

200.description: Plain-text original fields or Markdown returned directly; original JSON from R2 after following the default redirect

post.description: Return a receipt for each accepted job. JSON is the default; use Accept: text/plain for readable text. X-Respond-With is ignored here. To receive Markdown results, set that header when retrieving each completed job's results. Errors use JSON.

APIKeyIdentity.description: Authoritative current-record ownership and readiness. Public IDs only. recurringAllowed requires a verified active owner and, for agent-issued keys, server-confirmed installation. It is a point-in-time check, not an authorization token or permission to reuse cached data after revocation.

AgentPermission.description: Catalog-derived agent permissions. Trial eligibility is an explicit opt-in independent of owner approval. Storage and variable-price sources require owner access.

nextAction.description: Claim before the first data request when no requested source is trial eligible.

scopes.description: Actual scopes on the current API key. May be empty on an unowned claim-only connection; every data-source request is then forbidden.

requestedScopes.description: Original owner-access request. Claim approval can only reduce this set. Legacy connections retain their original scopes.

trialScopes.description: Saved subset eligible for the temporary key. Never expanded by catalog changes.

AgentCredentials.description: Sensitive ordinary API-key credentials. Never log or put in browser URLs. Proofs are returned on temporary registration; handoff returns the owned candidate key.

modes.description: Only modes backed by a real adapter or consumer in the current release

inputSchema.description: JSON Schema used by the Playground and generated clients

requiresStorageDestination.description: Whether query submission must include per-request storage configuration.

trialOffer.description: Current one-time trial allowance expressed as alternative PAYG usage amounts. Eligibility and approval are required. The amounts share one balance and are not additive. Null when a reliable estimate is unavailable. This is not an account eligibility decision or a promise of immediate credit issuance.

creditValueUsd.description: Fixed USD value of one credit, used to preview custom top-ups. The server computes the credited amount.

billingMessage.description: Stable, non-sensitive explanation suitable for the Pricing and Billing UI.

maxApiRequests.description: Maximum free API calls when the entire trial grant is spent on the lowest-cost per-request API at current Pay as you go rates. Other APIs may allow fewer calls. Downloads are billed by delivered bytes and excluded from this count.

googleSearchRequests.description: Requests if the entire grant is spent on Google sources, using the highest current source rate.

youtubeDataRequests.description: Standard YouTube requests, excluding Extended Search, using the highest current source rate.

downloadGigabytes.description: Approximate delivered media volume in decimal GB (1 GB = 1000000000 bytes). Zero when the grant cannot cover the initial download reservation. Completion also depends on per-job reservations and settlement.

includedCredits.description: Credits included in each paid subscription cycle; zero for Pay As You Go.

credits.description: Credits granted by a successful one-time top-up; zero for recurring prices.

googlePer1kCents.description: Google request price per 1,000 successful requests, in USD cents.

youtubePer1kCents.description: Standard YouTube request price per 1,000 successful requests, in USD cents.

downloadPerTbCents.description: Download price per decimal TB (1,000,000,000,000 bytes), in USD cents.

name.description: Optional display name. When omitted, defaults to the normalized email local part, truncated to 100 characters. Can be changed in the profile later.

termsVersion.description: Exact version rendered by the signup page; stale versions are rejected.

privacyVersion.description: Exact version rendered by the signup page; stale versions are rejected.

RegisterResponse.description: Generic receipt returned for both a new account and a recoverable pending account. It intentionally omits identity data to limit account enumeration.

rememberMe.description: Ignored for email_verification, legal_acceptance and deletion_recovery Sessions, which always use a short fixed expiry.

Account.description: Deleted accounts are only returned through authorized Admin projections; their identity fields are redacted.

AccountDeletionRequest.description: User-safe deletion summary. Durable processor cursor and per-step metadata are internal operational state and are intentionally omitted.

retryable.description: True only when an Admin-audited processor retry is possible; it does not grant the user mutation access.

UpdateOnboardingRequest.description: Server-owned resource state validates confirmation actions; clients never submit API Key or request IDs.

degradedSections.description: A listed section uses its unavailable representation; null and empty values must not be interpreted as zero or healthy.

Subscription.description: Effective entitlement projection. `status=payg` and `id=null` means no billing subscription record exists.

usageRates.description: Account-specific configured credit rates. Query rates come from the account entitlement, not the public plan catalog. One TB is 1,000,000,000,000 bytes; download charges are settled against actual bytes and rounded per result.

customized.description: True when an administrator configured rates for this account.

balanceCredits.description: Signed settled balance after grants, usage, refunds and provider reversals.

lifetimeRefundedCredits.description: Credits returned to the account after failed usage.

lifetimePaymentReversedCredits.description: Absolute Credits removed after verified provider refunds or chargebacks.

ApiKey.description: API key details. A key remains active until scheduledRevocationAt when revocation is scheduled.

scheduledRevocationAt.description: Planned revocation time for an overlapping retiring key; null for a primary or immediately revoked key.

secret.description: Plaintext secret returned only by this create/rotate transaction. Newly issued secrets use the `fd_` prefix. Previously issued `fd_test_` and `fd_live_` secrets still authenticate. An authenticated replay with the same Idempotency-Key and request body may receive the same KMS-encrypted response for five minutes; it is not recoverable afterward.

url.description: Provider-hosted HTTPS URL on a Stripe-controlled *.stripe.com host. Web clients must validate the origin and redirect from a server-only boundary.

id.description: FlashData subscription public ID. Entitlement still updates only after a verified provider event.

refundedAmount.description: Cumulative USD cents observed from verified provider events.

hostedInvoiceUrl.description: Stripe-hosted HTTPS invoice URL. Production Web clients accept only Stripe-controlled *.stripe.com origins.

BillingPayment.description: Account-scoped top-up projection. Refund state is updated only from verified provider events; this API does not initiate refunds.

hostedInvoiceUrl.description: Stripe-hosted HTTPS invoice URL, when Stripe created an invoice for this top-up.

reversedCredits.description: Cumulative credits removed by append-only payment_reversal entries; never exceeds credits.

result_origin.description: Configured signed-result storage origin, without credentials, path, query or fragment. Not an access token or a media URL.

balanceCredits.description: Signed live balance; in-flight reservations may already be reflected.

estimatedCredits.description: Null for downloads or missing pricing.

credits.description: Charged Credits in the current aggregate; pending work may not be finally settled.

refundHandling.description: Failed requests are refunded; verified provider refunds remove the proportional Credits through immutable transactions.

balanceAfterCredits.description: Signed settled balance after this immutable transaction, when recorded.

options.description: Reused for every ID. Metadata accepts include_formats and include_chapters. Transcript and captions accept language (one code or an array of 1–10 distinct codes) and auto (applies to all requested languages). Omit language to prefer en-orig, fall back to en, and return one track. With auto=true, each requested code tries its -orig track first, then the plain code. Explicit -orig codes and auto=false stay exact. languageCode identifies the selected track; requestedLanguageCode is included when it differs from the requested code. A language array returns tracks and per-language errors for each video; bulk exports remain JSONL, one record per video. Trainability accepts no source options. These four data sources optionally accept result_storage. Supported storage_type values are s3, s3_compatible, oss, gcs, azure, cos, bos, and tos. storage_url is the bucket name (Azure container name); object_prefix is optional. S3, S3-compatible, OSS, COS, BOS, and TOS use access_key and secret_key. S3-compatible and OSS also require a public HTTPS endpoint_url. COS, BOS, and TOS require region and use fixed provider endpoints. COS bucket names include the APPID. BOS S3-compatible HTTPS delivery supports bj, su, and hkg. GCS requires service_account with project_id, client_email, and private_key. Azure requires account_name and a container SAS sas_token with write permission. Default object_prefix is YYYYMMDD, frozen to the UTC bulk creation date. Files are written to <prefix>/<source>/<bulkId>/results/part-NNNNNNNN.jsonl.gz; manifest.json in the same bulk directory is written last. Each JSONL row includes its input index and completed, failed, or invalid status. Internal R2 results remain available through the result links for 24 hours. Download accepts the normal YouTube download parameters, requires customer storage, and does not permit browser_delivery. Download storage supports the same eight provider types and credential shapes listed above under the storage field. Download storage may include object_prefix; YYYYMMDD tokens resolve to the UTC upload date, while literal prefixes are unchanged.

callback_url.description: Optional public HTTPS endpoint notified once after manifest publication.

options.description: Partial option update. Nested storage fields are merged so unchanged credentials do not need to be resent. Data result_storage fields are merged the same way. After all IDs have been scanned, a paused data bulk job accepts credential updates only: access_key and secret_key, GCS service_account, or Azure sas_token, depending on the storage type. The complete merged configuration is validated before it is stored.

callback_url.description: Replacement completion callback, or null to remove the callback.

MarkdownQueryResult.description: Markdown result content. content replaces the results array; other response fields such as id, source, status, usage and timestamps are preserved. No generated summary is added. Source URLs and transcript segment start/end times are retained.

content.description: Deterministic Markdown derived from the retrieved source result.

ResponseEnvelopeAccept.name: Accept
ResponseEnvelopeAccept.description: application/json returns the original structured response; text/plain returns the same fields as indented plain text. Standard media ranges and q weights are supported; missing Accept or a global wildcard defaults to JSON. X-Respond-With is ignored on submission and job-status endpoints. Errors remain structured JSON. Both response types use UTF-8; an explicit charset=utf-8 parameter is supported.

QueryRepresentation.name: X-Respond-With
QueryRepresentation.description: Set to markdown to return result content as Markdown. Omit to retain the original result fields. Accept independently selects JSON or plain text. Only realtime queries and completed job result reads support this header. It does not change job submissions, status, account APIs, callbacks, Bulk files, binary downloads, or MCP protocol responses.

QueryRepresentationAccept.name: Accept
QueryRepresentationAccept.description: Select application/json or text/plain independently of X-Respond-With. Without X-Respond-With, text/plain returns the original fields with indentation; JSON retains the original response fields (completed-result reads redirect to storage). With markdown, JSON returns content plus metadata and plain text returns metadata followed by Markdown. Standard media ranges and q weights are supported; missing Accept or a global wildcard defaults to JSON. Both response types use UTF-8; an explicit charset=utf-8 parameter is supported.

dataApiKey.name: X-API-Key
dataApiKey.description: FlashData API key. Job access is restricted to the key's source scopes.

agentRegistrationProof.description: Persist a cryptographically random 32-byte base64url proof and exact request BEFORE sending; recover only with the same proof and body. Not an OAuth token.

cookieSession.name: __Host-fd_session
cookieSession.description: Opaque Web session. The browser cannot read this cookie.

agentSetupCredential.description: Temporary setup credential for status and claim creation only. Not a data API key.

agentIdentityKey.description: Ordinary FlashData API key in Authorization Bearer, only on agent identity. Data queries use X-API-Key instead.

agentHandoffProof.description: Proof used to recover the owner key and acknowledge installation. Never sent to a data query.
